name: Accusative + infinitive perception
explanation: After sehen or hören, the object can be followed directly by an infinitive: Ich sehe ihn gehen.

name: Indirect question
english: Question word + verb at the end
explanation: In an indirect question, the question word opens the clause and the finite verb goes to the end.

name: Conditional with würde
explanation: Use würde + infinitive for a hypothetical action.

name: Modal verb + infinitive at the end
english: The modal takes the personal ending in second position; the main verb waits, unconjugated, at the end of the clause.
explanation: The modal takes the personal ending in second position; the main verb waits, unconjugated, at the end of the clause.

name: Strong verb in the simple past
english: The vowel changes instead of adding -te. These have to be recognised, not derived.
explanation: The vowel changes instead of adding -te. These have to be recognised, not derived.

name: Reflexive verb with accusative sich
english: The verb needs sich to be complete. It is not translated in English, and it is not optional.
explanation: The verb needs sich to be complete. It is not translated in English, and it is not optional.

name: Separable verb, prefix split off
english: In a main clause the prefix detaches and travels to the end of the sentence, sometimes many words away from its verb.
explanation: In a main clause the prefix detaches and travels to the end of the sentence, sometimes many words away from its verb.

name: Subordinate clause with dass
english: dass sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: A dass-clause reports a thought or statement. The conjugated verb moves to the end.

name: Indirect yes/no question with ob
english: ob sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: Use ob for an indirect yes/no question. The finite verb goes to the end.

name: Subordinate clause: verb final
english: A subordinate conjunction sends the verb to the end
explanation: With bevor, während, als, wenn and similar conjunctions, the conjugated verb closes the clause.

name: Reason with weil
english: weil sends the finite verb to the end
explanation: Use weil to give a reason. The conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

name: Verb in second position
english: When something other than the subject opens the sentence, the verb still comes second and the subject moves behind it.
explanation: When something other than the subject opens the sentence, the verb still comes second and the subject moves behind it.

name: Infinitive with zu
english: zu + infinitive after verbs such as bitten and versuchen
explanation: Many verbs introduce another action with zu + infinitive.
